visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Revenue is 500 and cost of goods sold is 200. What is the gross margin?
questions.explain: Gross profit of 300 over revenue of 500 is 60%. 40% is cost of goods sold as a share of revenue, and 300 is the profit, not the margin.
questions.explain_at: And gross margin is six hundred over one thousand

questions.q: EBITDA is 100, depreciation 30, interest 20, tax rate 25%. What is net income?
questions.explain: EBIT of 70, minus 20 of interest, is 50 before tax; tax of 12.5 leaves 37.5. Skipping interest gives 52.5, skipping tax 50, skipping depreciation 60.
questions.explain_at: Tax at twenty-five percent is forty

options.text: No, the cash left when the asset was bought
Yes, fifty a year leaves the bank
Yes, once tax on it has been paid
No, it's paid when the asset wears out

questions.explain: The cash left once, on the day the machines were bought. Depreciation spreads that cost over their life, so no cash moves when it's booked.
questions.explain_at: Second trap. No. The cash went out once

questions.q: Which line on the income statement is what's left for shareholders?
questions.explain: Net income is what's left after the suppliers, staff, landlord, lenders and the tax authority have all been paid.
questions.explain_at: After the suppliers, the staff, the landlord

questions.q: A company adds its marketing costs back and calls it adjusted EBITDA. What's wrong?

options.text: Marketing is one-off, so it's fine
It removes a cost paid every year
It matters to bondholders, not owners

questions.explain: Marketing recurs every year and the business can't run without it, so adding it back overstates profit. That was the WeWork move.
questions.explain_at: The problem with WeWork was that it removed costs that recur
